title: oncall-temp-runbook-and-handoff-notes
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Night shift (2025-06-08 22:00 -> 2025-06-09 06:00)
- Primary issue: transient 503 spike for hosted-api (route /v1/generate) around 23:10-23:40 UTC; introduced increased latencies for a subset of small requests (~1k-2k rps).
- Root-cause hypothesis: autoscaler mis-judged instance warm pool due to new batching heuristic; see INF-4027 for details.
- Current state: system back to nominal after temporary mitigation; monitoring on watch.

Important incidents / timeline:
- 23:07 UTC: Pager fired (SLA-90 alert) \u2014 503 rate > 5% for 5m on region us-west1.
- 23:10 UTC: Investigated: observed CPU+IO burst on model-router-gpu nodes and many short-lived containers being created (high churn).
- 23:15 UTC: Rolled forward mitigation: increased min-replicas for serving-runtime pool in us-west1 from 4 -> 8 (k8s HPA override). Immediate drop in error rate. (See kubectl command below)
- 23:30 UTC: Reverted experimental batching config introduced by PR /serving-runtime@512 (GH link above) for canary traffic. Errors cleared by 23:38 UTC.
- 00:05 UTC: Post-mortem ticket created (INF-4027), assigned to Samir.

What I did / commands run (copyable):
- Check pods and restarts: 
  kubectl --context=prod-us-west1 get pods -n serving-runtime -o wide | grep model-router
  kubectl --context=prod-us-west1 describe pod <hot-pod> -n serving-runtime  # check events
- Increase min replicas (temporary override):
  kubectl --context=prod-us-west1 patch hpa model-router-hpa -n serving-runtime --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":8}]'
- Revert canary config: (rolled back canary deployment to v1.3.1)
  kubectl --context=prod-us-west1 rollout undo deploy/model-router-canary -n serving-runtime --to-revision=5
- Tail logs (filtered):
  kubectl --context=prod-us-west1 logs -n serving-runtime deploy/model-router --since=1h | grep -i error | tail -n 200
- Check autoscaler metrics (Grafana):
  grafana: dashboards/serving-runtime/autoscaler (bookmark)

Temporary runbook steps (for next on-call):
- If 503 spike returns:
  1) Verify error rate in SLO dashboard > threshold (SLA-90).
  2) Check model-router pods for restart loops and high cpu: kubectl get pods -n serving-runtime | grep model-router
  3) If churn + high cpu observed, increase minReplicas by +2 increments up to 10. Re-check errors for 5 min.
  4) If errors persist, rollback recent canary config / model changes (see linked GH PR).
  5) If still failing, escalate to SRE lead Samir Ali and on-call infra (Slack: @samir).

Persistent TODOs / follow-ups:
- INF-4027: full root-cause analysis (assigned to Samir) \u2014 include load trace and kernel scheduling debug logs.
- Add a guard in canary rollout pipeline to prevent autoscaler overrides when CPU/latency variance > 20%.
- Update runbook with exact kubectl patch snippet and reversal commands (this doc).
- Create synthetic load test to reproduce batching heuristic behavior (owner: eng-applied-ml).

Contacts / escalation:
- Primary SRE on-call: Samir Ali (@samir) \u2014 pager team lead
- Secondary: Jordan Lee (@jordan) \u2014 infra escalation
- Serving-runtime owner: Hazel Ortiz (eng-serving-runtime) \u2014 for model-router changes
- Product on-call (hosted-api): product-oncall@redwood.ai (email)

Notes to next on-call (informal):
- The batcher change in PR 512 looked promising for small requests but had a narrow window where instance scaling lagged. Keep an eye on the ratio of small->large sequences in the traffic histogram (dashboard: serving-runtime/seq-dist).
- If you need to rollback HPA changes, remember to run the patch with --type='json' (we burned time with a bad patch earlier tonight).
- If you hit a weird state where pods are terminating but HPA instantly creates new ones that fail liveness, try cordoning the node and draining to isolate the bad image. Only do this with Jordan's approval.

Quick checklist for handoff:
- [ ] Confirm alerts are green (SLA + infra)
- [ ] Leave any open tickets updated with timestamped actions
- [ ] Ensure INF-4027 has attachments: logs + commands used
- [ ] Ping Samir if you changed any overrides so they can be reverted during business hours

Misc / scratch notes (todo later):
- Consider adding an automated rollback to canary pipeline that triggers if error rate > 3% within 10m.
- Capture a run of p99 latency before and after autoscaler change for the postmortem.

End of notes. Feel free to edit this doc \u2014 it's rough. If you take over the shift, add a short summary line at the top with your name and time range.

-- Maya
